title: Microsoft has new AI privacy rules for schools
slides: Can Microsoft police AI in your child's classroom?
New privacy rules for schools using its AI tools
Teachers still can't see what students type into chatbots
Schools must now audit AI vendors — starting immediately
Ask your district: who reviews the algorithms?
thread_text:
1. Your kid's AI tutor has secrets

Microsoft can't see what students type into classroom chatbots. Privacy rules just changed, but the blind spot remains.

2. Schools signed a blank check

Districts now must audit every AI vendor they use — starting immediately. Most have no idea where to begin.

3. The audit nobody prepared for

Teachers were never given access to chatbot logs. So who checks if algorithms treat students fairly?

4. Vendors won't show their code

Companies call it proprietary. Schools call it a black box. Parents call it a problem.

5. Ask your district this week

Who reviews the algorithms your child's school uses? If no one knows, that's your answer.

instagram.caption:
Your child's school AI vendor just became your district's responsibility to audit — starting now.

Microsoft issued new privacy rules for schools using its AI tools. Districts must audit every AI vendor immediately.

But teachers still can't see what students type into classroom chatbots. Vendors call their algorithms proprietary. Schools call it a black box. 🔍

So who checks if these tools treat students fairly? 🤔

If you publish or create content involving schools, this sets a precedent for how AI transparency gets handled everywhere. 📋

Ask your district this week: who reviews the algorithms your child's school uses? If nobody knows, that's your answer. 💬
